court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Principal Family Court, Chennai (O.P.No.2137 of 2005 and O.P.No.2629 of 2009)
facts_of_case: The husband filed two divorce petitions against his wife, one for annulment and another for divorce due to mental cruelty. The trial court dismissed the first petition but allowed the second. Both parties appealed.

legal_principles.principle: The object of the Court is always to find out the truth.
legal_principles.held: After taking this Court through Ex.C-1, the Psychological Evaluation Report, the learned Counsel would rely upon the judgment in Sharda Vs. Dharmpal18 to contend that the object of the Court is always to find out the truth and the Courts, in matrimonial cases, can refer the parties to medical examination.
cited_cases: Sharda Vs. Dharmpal, (Year) X SCC Y
Lalith Kishore Vs. Meeru Sharma and Another, (Year) X SCC Z

legal_principles.principle: The Courts, in matrimonial cases, can refer the parties to medical examination.
legal_principles.held: the learned Counsel would rely upon the judgment in Lalith Kishore Vs. Meeru Sharma and Another19, more specifically relying upon paragraph Nos.4 and 5, would submit that the medical examination of the experts can only lead to the truth.
cited_cases: Lalith Kishore Vs. Meeru Sharma and Another, (Year) X SCC Z

legal_principles.principle: If the fault is on the part of the husband, then he is not entitled to relief.
legal_principles.held: he would submit that if the fault is on the part of the husband, then, by virtue of Section 23(i)(a) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, he is not entitled to relief.
cited_cases: T.Srinivasan Vs. T.Varalakshmi (Mrs), (Year) X SCC Y
Managaonkar Vs. Sunanda, (Year) X SCC Z

legal_principles.principle: The approach of the Court should be to preserve the matrimonial relationship.
legal_principles.held: he would submit that the approach of the Court should be to preserve the matrimonial relationship and should be reluctant to dissolve the marriage on the asking of one of the parties.
cited_cases: Savitri Pandey Vs. Prem Chandra Pandey, (Year) X SCC Y

outcome.result: Appeal allowed (C.M.A.No.2655 of 2019) / Appeal dismissed (C.M.A.No.2535 of 2019)
outcome.final_order: The appeal in C.M.A.No.2655 of 2019 was allowed, and the decree and judgment in O.P.No.2137 of 2005 were set aside. The appeal in C.M.A.No.2535 of 2019 was dismissed.

keywords: Latin Maxim: Actus non facit reum nisi mens sit rea
